name: Missouri

notes: Food eligible for SNAP (candy and soft drinks included) is taxed at a reduced 1.225% state rate plus the local rate on food, which the rate table gives (lower than the general local rate in St. Louis city and county and St. Charles County); hot or prepared food pays the full rate, which is not counted here.

Cigarettes and other tobacco are taxed at the full rate, on top of excise taxes left out here: 17 cents a pack of cigarettes and 10% of the invoice price on other tobacco; St. Louis County and Jackson County add their own cigarette taxes.
Household supplies: diapers and incontinence products have been exempt from state and local sales tax since August 28, 2025, which is not taken out here.
Personal care products: menstrual products have been exempt from state and local sales tax since August 28, 2025, which is not taken out here.
Barber and beauty services, laundry and dry cleaning, and auto repair labor: not taxed (FTA 2017 survey answer).

Clothing is taxed. The back-to-school sales tax holiday (August 7 to 9, 2026) exempted clothing of $100 or less an item, school supplies, computers and software up to set limits, which is not taken out here.
Home furnishings: the Show-Me Green sales tax holiday (April 19 to 25, 2026) exempted the first $1,500 of each Energy Star appliance, which is not taken out here.
Motor fuel is exempt from the sales tax and taxed by the gallon instead: 29.5 cents since July 1, 2025, left out here; drivers can claim a refund of the increases since 2021 for on-road fuel.
Hotel stays pay city and county lodging taxes (Kansas City 7.5% plus a $3-a-night arena fee, St. Louis 7.25%, Branson 4%), which are not counted here.
gaps: 20 cities whose DOR code differs from their Census code were matched by name.

47 cities lie in more than one county with a different rate in each county part; in each census tract such a city's rate is that of its part in the tract's county, counted for the share of the tract's store jobs located in the city.

Groceries pay the state's reduced 1.225% plus the local rate on food, which the rate table gives separately; it is lower than the general local rate in 109 places and counties (St. Louis city and St. Louis and St. Charles counties among them).

478 rate-table locations are not 2024 Census places and are left out: annexed parts of cities taxed at their own rate (for example "Ballwin (X1)") and unincorporated communities the DOR lists separately (for example Alley Springs). Their areas take the city or county rate here.

933 special-district combinations (community improvement, transportation development, ambulance, fire and other districts) are not applied; each covers part of a place or county. Rates of districts that cover a whole place or county are included.

Kansas City's 2% and Branson's 0.5% restaurant taxes are counted, as is the Branson/Lakes Area tourism district's 1% for Branson; St. Louis' 1.5% restaurant gross receipts tax is noted. Of the November 3, 2026 votes, by the election authorities' unofficial counts, St. Louis' Proposition B, Boone County's Proposition L and Blue Springs' use tax, Washburn's increase (by 4 votes), Indian Point's 0.5%, Purdy's use tax (by 15 votes) and Rockaway Beach's use tax failed; Houston Lake's use tax passed; the St. Charles County Ambulance District's 0.375%, Jackson County's COMBAT renewal, the Sni Valley Fire Protection District's 1%, Drexel's 0.5% increase and Johnson and Webster counties' continuations passed, and so did Polk County's new 0.5% for law enforcement; Humansville's use tax failed. Lee's Summit's question, on city-wide residential trash collection rather than a tax (Cass County's sample ballot), failed. The Gravois and Sunrise Beach fire protection districts' 1% taxes passed (from April 1, 2027 at the earliest), and so did Stover's use tax, by one vote. Each is noted on its page. Sample ballots read: St. Louis city and the Barry, Bates, Benton, Boone, Camden, Cass, Christian, Greene, Hickory, Howell, Jackson (with Kansas City's), Johnson, Lawrence, Miller, Morgan, Phelps, Platte, Polk, St. Charles, Stone, Taney and Webster counties. St. Louis County's and Clay County's weren't checked, and Drexel's question turned up only on a sample ballot read for another city, so the other counties' ballots may hold questions not yet found.

2907966: Branson's 0.5% tourism tax on food and drinks sold on restaurant premises is counted in its restaurant rate and on drinks served, since it reaches alcoholic drinks too (City of Branson; RSMo 94.805 allows it on restaurant food and drinks and on drinks at licensed bars); its 4% tourism tax on lodging and admissions is not.

The Branson/Lakes Area Tourism Community Enhancement District adds 1% (7/8% on restaurant meals; not on groceries) across most of Branson, all of Indian Point and parts of Branson West and Taney and Stone counties (Department of Revenue); it is counted for Branson (a small part of the city is outside it) and Indian Point, and left out elsewhere, where it covers only part of a place.

Enhanced enterprise zones are drawn for the 132 zones on the Department of Economic Development's current list (read November 2026), from the Department's block-group layers matched to the list by hand, and Kansas City's three from the City's own layer; four zones on the Department's layer that its list doesn't name (North and Central St. Louis County, the City of Macon and Stone County) aren't shown. The zones' own state tax credits are only for companies approved before August 23, 2013; the zones still carry local property-tax abatement and a zone category of the Missouri Works program.
